learn.title: Instructions for a computer
learn.body: A program is a list of instructions that a computer follows, one after another. Programming is the work of writing those instructions so the computer does a job for you, such as adding numbers, sorting names or drawing a game.

learn.title: Computers are literal
learn.body: A computer does exactly what you write, never what you meant. It cannot guess. If one instruction is missing or in the wrong place, the result is wrong. That is why programmers learn to be precise and to check their work.

learn.title: Source code
learn.body: The text you write is called source code. People can read it, but the processor cannot run it directly. The processor only understands machine code, which is long strings of ones and zeros.

learn.title: The compiler
learn.body: A compiler is a program that translates source code into machine code. In C you write source code, run the compiler, and get a new file you can run. C is popular because it is fast and shows you how computers really work.

learn.title: Idea to running program
learn.body: Here is the path every C program takes.
steps: You write source code in a file, for example `hello.c`
You run the compiler on that file
The compiler produces a runnable program, for example `hello`
You run that program and see what it does

learn.body: Read your own code slowly. The computer will follow every instruction literally, so you should too.
